passages.text: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh and told them, “You have done all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the leader of Israel after Moses.
Joshua called the Reubenites.
Joshua called the Gadites.
Joshua called the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Joshua spoke to them.
Joshua said, “You have obeyed everything Moses commanded you.
Moses was the servant of the LORD.
You have also listened to me.
You have done everything I commanded you.”
passages.original: אָ֚ז יִקְרָ֣א יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֖י וְלַגָּדִ֑י וְלַחֲצִ֖י מַטֵּ֥ה מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אַתֶּ֣ם שְׁמַרְתֶּ֔ם אֵ֚ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֔ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֣בֶד יְהוָ֑ה וַתִּשְׁמְע֣וּ בְקוֹלִ֔י לְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: All this time you have not deserted your brothers, up to this very day, but have kept the charge given you by the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh are the subject.
You have not deserted your brothers.
You have stayed with them for many days.
You have remained with them until this very day.
You have kept the command of the LORD your God.
You have obeyed what the LORD your God required of you.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־ אֲחֵיכֶ֗ם זֶ֚ה יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֕ם אֶת־ מִשְׁמֶ֕רֶת מִצְוַ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And now that the LORD your God has given your brothers rest as He promised them, you may return to your homes in the land that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you across the Jordan.
passages.sermon:
Joshua spoke to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The LORD is your God.
The LORD has given your brothers rest.
The LORD did what He promised to your brothers.
Now you may go back to your homes.
Go to the land that belongs to you.
Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you this land.
This land is across the Jordan River.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֵנִ֨יחַ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ לַֽאֲחֵיכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וְעַתָּ֡ה פְּנוּ֩ וּלְכ֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם לְאָהֳלֵיכֶ֗ם אֶל־ אֶ֙רֶץ֙ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ נָתַ֣ן לָכֶ֗ם מֹשֶׁה֙ עֶ֣בֶד יְהוָ֔ה בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

passages.text: But be very careful to observe the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to hold fast to Him, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the servant of the LORD.
Moses gave you the commandment and the law.
Be very careful to obey them.
Love the LORD your God.
Walk in all His ways.
Keep His commandments.
Hold fast to Him.
Serve Him with all your heart.
Serve Him with all your soul.
passages.original: רַ֣ק׀ שִׁמְר֣וּ מְאֹ֗ד לַעֲשׂ֨וֹת אֶת־ הַמִּצְוָ֣ה וְאֶת־ הַתּוֹרָה֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה אֶתְכֶם֮ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־ יְהוָה֒ לְ֠אַהֲבָה אֶת־ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֜ם וְלָלֶ֧כֶת בְּכָל־ דְּרָכָ֛יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֥ר מִצְוֺתָ֖יו וּלְדָבְקָה־ ב֑וֹ וּלְעָבְד֕וֹ בְּכָל־ לְבַבְכֶ֖ם וּבְכָל־ נַפְשְׁכֶֽם׃

passages.text: So Joshua blessed them and sent them on their way, and they went to their homes.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the leader of Israel.
Joshua blessed the people.
Joshua sent the people away.
The people went to their homes.
passages.original: וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֖ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אֶל־ אָהֳלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: (To the half-tribe of Manasseh Moses had given land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave land on the west side of the Jordan among their brothers.) When Joshua sent them to their homes he blessed them, saying, “Return to your homes with your great wealth, with immense herds of livestock, with silver, gold, bronze, iron, and very many clothes. Divide with your brothers the spoil of your enemies.”
passages.sermon:
Moses gave land in Bashan to half of the tribe of Manasseh.
Joshua gave land to the other half of Manasseh on the west side of the Jordan.
Their brothers lived there.
Joshua sent the people of Manasseh to their homes.
Joshua blessed them.
Joshua said to them, “Return to your homes with your great wealth.
You have many herds of livestock.
You have silver, gold, bronze, and iron.
You have very many clothes.
Share the spoil of your enemies with your brothers.”
passages.original: וְלַחֲצִ֣י׀ שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֗ה נָתַ֣ן מֹשֶׁה֮ בַּבָּשָׁן֒ וּלְחֶצְי֗וֹ נָתַ֤ן יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ עִם־ אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם מֵעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה וְ֠גַם כִּ֣י שִׁלְּחָ֧ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל־ אָהֳלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיְבָרֲכֵֽם׃ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר בִּנְכָסִ֨ים רַבִּ֜ים שׁ֤וּבוּ אֶל־ אָֽהֳלֵיכֶם֙ וּבְמִקְנֶ֣ה רַב־ מְאֹ֔ד בְּכֶ֨סֶף וּבְזָהָ֜ב וּבִנְחֹ֧שֶׁת וּבְבַרְזֶ֛ל וּבִשְׂלָמ֖וֹת הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד חִלְק֥וּ שְׁלַל־ אֹיְבֵיכֶ֖ם עִם־ אֲחֵיכֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: So the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan to return to their own land of Gilead, which they had acquired according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were tribes of Israel.
They had been staying with the other Israelites at Shiloh.
Shiloh was in the land of Canaan.
They left the Israelites at Shiloh.
They traveled to the land of Gilead.
Gilead was their own land.
They had received Gilead as their possession.
They received this land because the LORD commanded it.
Moses gave them this land by the LORD’s command.
passages.original: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ וַיֵּלְכ֡וּ בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֨ן וּבְנֵי־ גָ֜ד וַחֲצִ֣י׀ שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֗ה מֵאֵת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִשִּׁלֹ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ כְּנָ֑עַן לָלֶ֜כֶת אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֗ד אֶל־ אֶ֤רֶץ אֲחֻזָּתָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֹֽאחֲזוּ־ בָ֔הּ עַל־ פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: And when they came to Geliloth near the Jordan in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an imposing altar there by the Jordan.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were Israelite tribes.
They traveled to Geliloth.
Geliloth is near the Jordan River.
Geliloth is in the land of Canaan.
They arrived at Geliloth.
They built an altar there.
They built the altar by the Jordan River.
The altar was very large and impressive.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־ גְּלִיל֣וֹת הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַיִּבְנ֣וּ בְנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֣ן וּבְנֵי־ גָ֡ד וַחֲצִ֣י שֵׁבֶט֩ הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֨ה שָׁ֤ם מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ עַל־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן מִזְבֵּ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל לְמַרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then the Israelites received the report: “Behold, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar on the border of the land of Canaan, at Geliloth near the Jordan on the Israelite side.”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites heard a report.
The report said something important.
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar.
They built this altar on the border of the land of Canaan.
They built it at Geliloth, near the Jordan River.
They built it on the side that belongs to the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמְע֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה בָנ֣וּ בְנֵֽי־ רְאוּבֵ֣ן וּבְנֵי־ גָ֡ד וַחֲצִי֩ שֵׁ֨בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֶת־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ אֶל־ מוּל֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֶל־ גְּלִילוֹת֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֶל־ עֵ֖בֶר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And when they heard this, the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh to go to war against them.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites heard the report.
The Israelites were the people God chose.
All the Israelites gathered together at Shiloh.
They gathered as one group.
They prepared to go to war against the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּקָּ֨הֲל֜וּ כָּל־ עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שִׁלֹ֔ה לַעֲל֥וֹת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לַצָּבָֽא׃פ

passages.text: The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the land of Gilead, to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites acted together as a group.
They sent a man named Phinehas.
Phinehas was the son of Eleazar.
Eleazar was a priest.
The Israelites sent Phinehas to the land of Gilead.
They sent him to the Reubenites.
They sent him to the Gadites.
They sent him to the half-tribe of Manasseh.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־ בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֧ן וְאֶל־ בְּנֵי־ גָ֛ד וְאֶל־ חֲצִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־ מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֑ד אֶת־ פִּינְחָ֖ס בֶּן־ אֶלְעָזָ֥ר הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: With him they sent ten chiefs—one family leader from each tribe of Israel, each the head of a family among the clans of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites sent ten chiefs with Phinehas.
Each chief came from a different tribe of Israel.
Each chief was the leader of a family group in his tribe.
Each chief was the head of his father's house among the clans of Israel.
passages.original: וַעֲשָׂרָ֤ה נְשִׂאִים֙ עִמּ֔וֹ נָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד נָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙ לְבֵ֣ית אָ֔ב לְכֹ֖ל מַטּ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאִ֨ישׁ רֹ֧אשׁ בֵּית־ אֲבוֹתָ֛ם הֵ֖מָּה לְאַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: They went to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead and said to them, “This is what the whole congregation of the LORD says: ‘What is this breach of faith you have committed today against the God of Israel by turning away from the LORD and building for yourselves an altar, that you might rebel against the LORD this day?
passages.sermon:
Phinehas was a priest and the son of Eleazar.
The Israelites sent Phinehas to the land of Gilead.
He went with ten chiefs.
Each chief was a leader from a tribe of Israel.
They went to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
These tribes lived in the land of Gilead.
Phinehas and the chiefs spoke to them.
They said, “The whole congregation of the LORD speaks to you.
What is this breach of faith you have committed today against the God of Israel?
You have turned away from the LORD.
You have built an altar for yourselves.
You have rebelled against the LORD today.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל־ בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֧ן וְאֶל־ בְּנֵי־ גָ֛ד וְאֶל־ חֲצִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־ מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֑ד וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אִתָּ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּ֣ה אָמְר֞וּ כֹּ֣ל׀ עֲדַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה מָֽה־ הַמַּ֤עַל הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר מְעַלְתֶּם֙ בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָשׁ֣וּב הַיּ֔וֹם מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה בִּבְנֽוֹתְכֶ֤ם לָכֶם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לִמְרָדְכֶ֥ם הַיּ֖וֹם בַּיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Was not the sin of Peor enough for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day? It even brought a plague upon the congregation of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites sinned at Peor.
This sin was very serious.
We have not cleansed ourselves from this sin until today.
Because of this sin, a plague came upon the congregation of the LORD.
passages.original: הַמְעַט־ לָ֙נוּ֙ אֶת־ עֲוֺ֣ן פְּע֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ הִטַּהַ֙רְנוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְהִ֥י הַנֶּ֖גֶף בַּעֲדַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And now, would you turn away from the LORD? If you rebel today against the LORD, tomorrow He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Israel spoke to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
They said, “You are turning away from the LORD today.
If you rebel against the LORD today, He will be angry.
Tomorrow, He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.”
passages.original: וְאַתֶּם֙ תָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַיּ֔וֹם מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֗ה אַתֶּ֞ם תִּמְרְד֤וּ הַיּוֹם֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּמָחָ֕ר אֶֽל־ כָּל־ עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִקְצֹֽף׃

passages.text: If indeed the land of your inheritance is unclean, then cross over to the land of the LORD’s possession, where the LORD’s tabernacle stands, and take possession of it among us. But do not rebel against the LORD or against us by building for yourselves an altar other than the altar of the LORD our God.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Israel spoke to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
They said, “If your land of inheritance is unclean, come over to the land that belongs to the LORD.
This is the land where the LORD’s tabernacle stands.
Take possession of land among us.
Do not rebel against the LORD.
Do not rebel against us.
Do not build an altar for yourselves apart from the altar of the LORD our God.”
passages.original: וְאַ֨ךְ אִם־ טְמֵאָ֜ה אֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֗ם עִבְר֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם אֶל־ אֶ֨רֶץ אֲחֻזַּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָֽׁכַן־ שָׁם֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵאָחֲז֖וּ בְּתוֹכֵ֑נוּ וּבַֽיהוָ֣ה אַל־ תִּמְרֹ֗דוּ וְאֹתָ֙נוּ֙ אֶל־ תִּמְרֹ֔דוּ בִּבְנֹֽתְכֶ֤ם לָכֶם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ מִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֔י מִזְבַּ֖ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Was not Achan son of Zerah unfaithful regarding what was set apart for destruction, bringing wrath upon the whole congregation of Israel? Yet it was not only Achan who perished because of his sin!’ ”
passages.sermon:
Achan was the son of Zerah.
Achan acted unfaithfully.
He took things that were set apart for destruction.
Because of Achan’s sin, God became angry.
God’s anger came upon the whole congregation of Israel.
Achan was only one man.
But Achan was not the only one who suffered for his sin.
passages.original: הֲל֣וֹא׀ עָכָ֣ן בֶּן־ זֶ֗רַח מָ֤עַל מַ֙עַל֙ בַּחֵ֔רֶם וְעַֽל־ כָּל־ עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הָ֣יָה קָ֑צֶף וְהוּא֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד לֹ֥א גָוַ֖ע בַּעֲוֺנֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Then the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the clans of Israel: “The LORD, the Mighty One, is God! The LORD, the Mighty One, is God! He knows, and may Israel also know. If this was in rebellion or breach of faith against the LORD, do not spare us today.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh spoke to the leaders of the clans of Israel.
They said, “The LORD is God.
The LORD is the Mighty One.
He is God.
The LORD knows the truth.
Let Israel also know the truth.
If we have rebelled against the LORD, do not spare us today.
If we have been unfaithful to the LORD, do not save us today.”
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲנוּ֙ בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֣ן וּבְנֵי־ גָ֔ד וַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶת־ רָאשֵׁ֖י אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ אֵל֩׀ אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀ יְהוָ֜ה אֵ֣ל׀ אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀ יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא יֹדֵ֔עַ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע אִם־ בְּמֶ֤רֶד וְאִם־ בְּמַ֙עַל֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה אַל־ תּוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: If we have built for ourselves an altar to turn away from Him and to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings on it, or to sacrifice fellowship offerings on it, may the LORD Himself hold us accountable.
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh spoke to the leaders of Israel.
They said, “If we built an altar for ourselves to turn away from the LORD, He knows it.
If we built this altar to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings on it, the LORD knows it.
If we built this altar to sacrifice fellowship offerings on it, the LORD knows it.
If we did any of these things, may the LORD Himself hold us accountable.”
passages.original: לִבְנ֥וֹת לָ֙נוּ֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לָשׁ֖וּב מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאִם־ לְהַעֲל֨וֹת עָלָ֜יו עוֹלָ֣ה וּמִנְחָ֗ה וְאִם־ לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת עָלָיו֙ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֔ים יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא יְבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

passages.text: But in fact we have done this for fear that in the future your descendants might say to ours, ‘What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar.
They did not build it out of rebellion.
They did not build it to turn away from the LORD.
They built it because they were afraid of something.
They feared what might happen in the future.
They thought your descendants might speak to our descendants.
They thought your descendants might say, “What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?”
They wanted to prevent this from happening.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֤א מִדְּאָגָה֙ מִדָּבָ֔ר עָשִׂ֥ינוּ אֶת־ זֹ֖את לֵאמֹ֑ר מָחָ֗ר יֹאמְר֨וּ בְנֵיכֶ֤ם לְבָנֵ֙ינוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַה־ לָּכֶ֕ם וְלַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For the LORD has made the Jordan a border between us and you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in the LORD!’ So your descendants could cause ours to stop fearing the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD set a border between us and you.
We are the Israelites west of the Jordan.
You are the Reubenites and Gadites east of the Jordan.
The LORD made the Jordan River this border.
You have no share in the LORD.
Your descendants could tell our descendants this.
Your descendants could make our descendants stop fearing the LORD.
passages.original: וּגְב֣וּל נָֽתַן־ יְ֠הוָה בֵּינֵ֨נוּ וּבֵינֵיכֶ֜ם בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֤ן וּבְנֵי־ גָד֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֵין־ לָכֶ֥ם חֵ֖לֶק בַּֽיהוָ֑ה וְהִשְׁבִּ֤יתוּ בְנֵיכֶם֙ אֶת־ בָּנֵ֔ינוּ לְבִלְתִּ֖י יְרֹ֥א אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: That is why we said, ‘Let us take action and build an altar for ourselves, but not for burnt offerings or sacrifices.
passages.sermon:
We are the people of Reuben and Gad.
We spoke to the other tribes of Israel.
We said, “Let us build an altar for ourselves.
We will not use this altar for burnt offerings.
We will not use this altar for sacrifices.”
passages.original: וַנֹּ֕אמֶר נַעֲשֶׂה־ נָּ֣א לָ֔נוּ לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ לֹ֥א לְעוֹלָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א לְזָֽבַח׃

passages.text: Rather, let it be a witness between us and you and the generations to come, that we will worship the LORD in His presence with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings.’ Then in the future, your descendants cannot say to ours, ‘You have no share in the LORD!’
passages.sermon:
This altar stands as a witness.
It stands between us and you.
It stands between our descendants and your descendants.
It shows that we worship the LORD.
We worship the LORD in His presence.
We bring our burnt offerings to Him.
We bring our sacrifices to Him.
We bring our peace offerings to Him.
This witness prevents future disputes.
Your descendants cannot say to our descendants, “You have no share in the LORD.”
passages.original: כִּי֩ עֵ֨ד ה֜וּא בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֵיכֶ֗ם וּבֵ֣ין דֹּרוֹתֵינוּ֮ אַחֲרֵינוּ֒ לַעֲבֹ֞ד אֶת־ עֲבֹדַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ לְפָנָ֔יו בְּעֹלוֹתֵ֥ינוּ וּבִזְבָחֵ֖ינוּ וּבִשְׁלָמֵ֑ינוּ וְלֹא־ יֹאמְר֨וּ בְנֵיכֶ֤ם מָחָר֙ לְבָנֵ֔ינוּ אֵין־ לָכֶ֥ם חֵ֖לֶק בַּיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Therefore we said, ‘If they ever say this to us or to our descendants, we will answer: Look at the replica of the altar of the LORD that our fathers made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.’
passages.sermon:
The people of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh spoke.
They said, “If anyone speaks to us or to our children in the future, we will answer them.
We will say, ‘Look at the copy of the altar of the LORD.
Our fathers made this altar.
They did not make it for burnt offerings.
They did not make it for sacrifices.
This altar stands as a witness between us and you.’”
passages.original: וַנֹּ֕אמֶר וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־ יֹאמְר֥וּ אֵלֵ֛ינוּ וְאֶל־ דֹּרֹתֵ֖ינוּ מָחָ֑ר וְאָמַ֡רְנוּ רְא֣וּ אֶת־ תַּבְנִית֩ מִזְבַּ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ לֹ֤א לְעוֹלָה֙ וְלֹ֣א לְזֶ֔בַח כִּי־ עֵ֣ד ה֔וּא בֵּינֵ֖ינוּ וּבֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away from Him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices, other than the altar of the LORD our God, which stands before His tabernacle.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh spoke.
They said, “We will not rebel against the LORD.
We will not turn away from the LORD today.
We will not build an altar for burnt offerings.
We will not build an altar for grain offerings.
We will not build an altar for sacrifices.
We will only use the altar of the LORD our God.
This altar stands before His tabernacle.
We will not use any other altar.”
passages.original: חָלִילָה֩ לָּ֨נוּ מִמֶּ֜נּוּ לִמְרֹ֣ד בַּֽיהוָ֗ה וְלָשׁ֤וּב הַיּוֹם֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לִבְנ֣וֹת מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לְעֹלָ֖ה לְמִנְחָ֣ה וּלְזָ֑בַח מִלְּבַ֗ד מִזְבַּח֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י מִשְׁכָּנֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: When Phinehas the priest and the chiefs of the congregation—the heads of Israel’s clans who were with him—heard what the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh had to say, they were satisfied.
passages.sermon:
Phinehas was a priest of Israel.
The chiefs of the congregation were with him.
These chiefs were the heads of Israel’s clans.
Phinehas and the chiefs listened to the words of the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh.
The descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh spoke to them.
Phinehas and the chiefs heard what they said.
Phinehas and the chiefs were satisfied with their words.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע פִּֽינְחָ֣ס הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וּנְשִׂיאֵ֨י הָעֵדָ֜ה וְרָאשֵׁ֨י אַלְפֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ אֶת־ הַ֨דְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר דִּבְּר֛וּ בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֥ן וּבְנֵי־ גָ֖ד וּבְנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַיִּיטַ֖ב בְּעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, “Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this breach of faith against Him. Consequently, you have delivered the Israelites from the hand of the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Phinehas was the son of Eleazar.
Phinehas was a priest.
Phinehas spoke to the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh.
Phinehas said, “Today we know something important.
We know that the LORD is among us.
You did not commit a breach of faith against the LORD.
You did not betray Him in this matter.
Because of this, you have saved the Israelites.
You have delivered them from the hand of the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פִּֽינְחָ֣ס בֶּן־ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֡ן אֶל־ בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֨ן וְאֶל־ בְּנֵי־ גָ֜ד וְאֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה הַיּ֤וֹם׀ יָדַ֙עְנוּ֙ כִּֽי־ בְתוֹכֵ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ מְעַלְתֶּ֥ם בַּֽיהוָ֖ה הַמַּ֣עַל הַזֶּ֑ה אָ֗ז הִצַּלְתֶּ֛ם אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, together with the other leaders, returned to the Israelites in the land of Canaan and brought back a report regarding the Reubenites and Gadites in the land of Gilead.
passages.sermon:
Phinehas was the son of Eleazar.
Phinehas was a priest.
The leaders of Israel were with Phinehas.
Phinehas and the leaders had been with the descendants of Reuben and Gad.
The descendants of Reuben and Gad lived in the land of Gilead.
Phinehas and the leaders left the land of Gilead.
They returned to the land of Canaan.
They went to the Israelites in Canaan.
Phinehas and the leaders brought back a report.
The report was about the descendants of Reuben and Gad.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣שָׁב פִּֽינְחָ֣ס בֶּן־ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֣ן׀ וְהַנְּשִׂיאִ֡ים מֵאֵ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־ רְאוּבֵן֩ וּמֵאֵ֨ת בְּנֵי־ גָ֜ד מֵאֶ֧רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֛ד אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנַ֖עַן אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּשִׁ֥בוּ אוֹתָ֖ם דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: The Israelites were satisfied with the report, and they blessed God and spoke no more about going to war against them to destroy the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites heard the report.
The report pleased the Israelites.
The Israelites blessed God.
The Israelites decided not to go to war against the Reubenites and Gadites.
The Israelites did not plan to destroy the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.
passages.original: וַיִּיטַ֣ב הַדָּבָ֗ר בְּעֵינֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְבָרֲכ֥וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֣א אָמְר֗וּ לַעֲל֤וֹת עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לְשַׁחֵת֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֥ן וּבְנֵי־ גָ֖ד יֹשְׁבִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: So the Reubenites and Gadites named the altar Witness, for they said, “It is a witness between us that the LORD is God.”
passages.sermon:
The Reubenites and the Gadites built an altar.
They gave the altar a name.
They called the altar Witness.
They said, “This altar is a witness between us.”
They said, “The LORD is God.”
passages.original: וַֽיִּקְרְא֛וּ בְּנֵי־ רְאוּבֵ֥ן וּבְנֵי־ גָ֖ד לַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כִּ֣י עֵ֥ד הוּא֙ בֵּֽינֹתֵ֔ינוּ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃פ
